seams.title: 1 supplier(s) process customer data outside UK/EEA, against the customer terms

facts.promise: Customer payment data is processed and stored only within the UK or EEA, including by sub-processors.
breaches: V002 StreamLedger Inc: customer payment data processed in US-East (United States); C-2026-031 DPA signed=True

seams.explanation: Our customer terms promise that customer payment data is processed and stored only within the UK or EEA, including by sub-processors. However, supplier V002 StreamLedger Inc processes customer payment data in US-East (United States), which breaks that promise even though its DPA (C-2026-031) is signed. Finance, Legal and Product each own part of this, so the gap sits between teams and needs a joint decision before launch.
fix_options: Product and Finance ask StreamLedger Inc to move processing of our customer payment data to a UK or EEA region. Legal then confirms the change under DPA C-2026-031.
Finance and Product replace StreamLedger Inc with a supplier that processes customer payment data only in the UK or EEA.
Legal revises the customer terms to disclose and permit processing in the United States by sub-processors. This only works if the business accepts changing the promise to customers.
basis: Contract: Customer Terms v2.0 clause 7.2 (UK/EEA only)
EU law: GDPR Ch. V transfers; DORA Art. 30(2)(b) processing locations

seams.title: Approval APR-2026-014 covers v1.4 but QuickPay launches v2.0 with 3 material change(s) and no change control request

material_changes: CHG-01 Cross-border payments to EU beneficiaries (new_feature)
CHG-02 Transaction analytics and fraud scoring via StreamLedger (new_third_party_processor)
CHG-03 Premium support tier with 24x7 support (new_service_commitment)

seams.explanation: Legal's approval APR-2026-014 covers QuickPay version 1.4, but Product is launching version 2.0, which adds 3 material changes: cross-border payments to EU beneficiaries (CHG-01), transaction analytics and fraud scoring via the new third-party processor StreamLedger (CHG-02), and a 24x7 premium support tier (CHG-03). No change control request has been filed for these changes. The approval remains valid until 2027-06-12, but only for v1.4, so v2.0 is currently launching without approval.
fix_options: Product files a change control request covering CHG-01, CHG-02 and CHG-03 so Legal can review them and amend APR-2026-014, or issue a new approval, to cover v2.0 before launch.
Delay the v2.0 launch until Legal approves v2.0. Until then, keep v1.4 live under the existing APR-2026-014 approval.

Launch only the scope already approved by disabling the three material changes (EU cross-border payments, StreamLedger analytics and fraud scoring, and the 24x7 premium support tier). Then release each one only after change control is filed and Legal approves it.
basis: Internal policy: Product Change Control Policy 2
EU law: DORA Art. 9 ICT change management

seams.title: Meera Iyer leaves on 2026-11-27 but still holds 7 role(s) needed at launch

roles: owner of OBL-L-001: Each payments product must hold a current, unexpired Legal approval.
owner of OBL-L-003: Customer payment data is processed and stored only within the UK or EE
owner of OBL-L-006: The regulator is notified at least five business days before launching
accountable senior manager on approval APR-2026-014 for QuickPay
sole approver for 'QuickPay product spend' (limit 250,000, no delegate)
approver of pending PO-2026-0450 (45,000, Launch monitoring and on-call tooling)
obligations: Each payments product must hold a current, unexpired Legal approval.
Customer payment data is processed and stored only within the UK or EEA, including by sub-processors.
The regulator is notified at least five business days before launching a new payments feature.

seams.explanation: Meera Iyer, Head of Payments Product, leaves on 2026-11-27, four days before the 2026-12-01 launch, but she still holds 7 roles the launch depends on across Legal, Finance, HR and Product. These roles are: owner of three Legal obligations (OBL-L-001 Legal approval, OBL-L-003 UK/EEA data location, OBL-L-006 regulator notification at least five business days before launch); accountable senior manager on approval APR-2026-014 for QuickPay; product owner of QuickPay; sole approver for 'QuickPay product spend' (limit 250,000) with no delegate; and approver of pending PO-2026-0450 (45,000, launch monitoring and on-call tooling). Once she leaves, each of these will have no owner, and the spend approval will have no backup.
fix_options: Before 2026-11-27, name successors and formally reassign ownership of OBL-L-001, OBL-L-003 and OBL-L-006, the product owner role for QuickPay, and the accountable senior manager role on APR-2026-014 (Legal, Product and HR to confirm the handover).

Have Finance add a delegate or replacement approver for 'QuickPay product spend' (limit 250,000), and get pending PO-2026-0450 (45,000) either approved by Meera before she leaves or reassigned to the new approver.
If successors cannot be confirmed before 2026-11-27, escalate a decision on holding the 2026-12-01 launch until every one of the 7 roles has an active owner.
basis: EU law: GDPR Art. 5(2) accountability; DORA Art. 5
Internal policy: HR 6.2 leaver handover; Finance 3.3 ASM approval

seams.title: Promised 336 staffed hours/week but staffing covers 240; Support hiring frozen until 2027-03-31

facts.promise: Premium customers receive 24x7 support, with at least two agents staffed at all times and a first response within 15 minutes for payment failures.
budget_coverage: B-001 Support staff (6 FTE): Business hours Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00; no out-of-hours line

seams.explanation: The promise to Premium customers requires 336 staffed agent-hours per week (24x7 support, at least two agents at all times, and a 15-minute first response for payment failures), but the 6 budgeted support staff provide only 240 hours, leaving a 96-hour weekly gap. The budget line (B-001) covers only business hours, Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00, with no out-of-hours line, so nights and weekends have no coverage at all. HR cannot close the gap by hiring because Support hiring is frozen until 2027-03-31.
fix_options: Legal revises the Premium promise to match funded coverage (business hours Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00) and removes or rescopes the 24x7, two-agent, and 15-minute payment-failure commitments before launch.
Finance funds an out-of-hours support line, and HR seeks an exception to the hiring freeze, to cover the 96-hour weekly gap, including nights and weekends.
Delay the 24x7 Premium commitment until Support hiring reopens after 2027-03-31, and launch now with only the support terms the current 6-agent staffing can meet.
basis: Contract: Customer Terms v2.0 clause 9.1 (24x7, two agents)

seams.title: 3 seller(s) will not hold valid PCT-101 on their first sales date

facts.requirement: Only employees holding valid Payments Conduct Training (PCT-101, 12 months) may sell or onboard customers to a payments product.
sellers_without_valid_training: E013 Ben Foster: PCT-101 expires 2026-11-25, first sale 2026-12-01
E014 Chloe Dubois: PCT-101 not started, first sale 2026-12-01
E015 Dmitri Volkov: PCT-101 not started, first sale 2026-12-01

seams.explanation: Legal requires that only employees holding valid Payments Conduct Training (PCT-101, valid for 12 months) may sell or onboard customers to a payments product, but HR's mandatory training list does not include PCT-101. As a result, 3 sellers scheduled to make their first sales on 2026-12-01 will not be compliant: Ben Foster's (E013) PCT-101 expires on 2026-11-25, and Chloe Dubois (E014) and Dmitri Volkov (E015) have not started the course.
fix_options: Get E013 Ben Foster to renew PCT-101 before it expires on 2026-11-25, and get E014 Chloe Dubois and E015 Dmitri Volkov to complete PCT-101 before their first sale date of 2026-12-01.

Hold back any seller who does not have valid PCT-101 from selling or onboarding payments customers until they complete the course. This means delaying their 2026-12-01 start rather than letting them sell without valid training.
Have HR add PCT-101 to its mandatory training list so that Legal's requirement is tracked and enforced automatically, and future sellers do not reach a first sale date without valid training.
basis: Internal policy: Conduct Policy 5.3 (PCT-101 on date of sale)
EU law: GDPR Art. 39(1)(b) staff training
